review:
[BLOCKING] `orders/service.py:94`, in `OrderService.dispatch`: the caller still relies on the old contract, where `send` raised `NotifyError`. It calls `self.notifier.send(...)` and ignores the return value. The `except NotifyError` branch is now dead code.

Take a courier SMS that the provider rejects, for example because of a bad number or a timeout. `send` now returns `False`. `dispatch` doesn't check that, so it never calls `self.outbox.add(...)`. The courier is never told about the pickup, and the order is already `OUT_FOR_DELIVERY`. The retry worker has nothing to retry, so the failure ends up as one warning line in the log. `dispatch` returns normally.

Fix it by changing `dispatch` to `if not self.notifier.send(...): self.outbox.add(order.courier_id, text)`. Also remove the stale `NotifyError` import and handler.

[NIT] `orders/notify.py:17`: the `Notifier` docstring now says `send` returns `False` on a provider timeout. The code only handles `resp.ok` being false. If `self.sms.send` raises on a timeout, the exception still propagates. In that case `dispatch` would no longer catch it either, because it only catches `NotifyError`. Confirm how the SMS client reports timeouts.

[NIT] `tests/test_service.py`: `FakeNotifier` doesn't model the new return value, so no test covers the failure path. A test where `send` returns `False` would have caught the blocking issue above.
